title: Больной Родион в куртке Кости  (Sick Rodion in Kostya's Jacket)

segments.t: Stepping out into the courtyard for a break, Kostya is outraged to spot Rodion Sergeyevich wearing his favorite jacket and demands he take it off at once. Nastya rushes out to stop Kostya, explaining that she lent Rodion the jacket because the poor man has caught a bad cold out in the freezing air.
Это я дала ему твою куртку.
Он еще и больной, что ли, с ним?
Значит, может мне тоже по помойкам лазить?
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'That is my jacket.' Notice how Russian expresses 'this' and 'jacket' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Take it off right now.' Max anchors the line on 'and', while 'take off' completes the thought.
'Come on, take it off, you thief!' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'go on' and finishing on 'crook'. Max answers right away.
'Keep talking, thief, take it off right now.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'talk' before landing on 'let's'.
Это я дала ему твою куртку.
'I was the one who gave him your jacket.' Kostya anchors the line on 'this', while 'jacket' completes the thought.
'Kostya, stop it right now!' An emphatic spoken line centered on the verb meaning 'stop it'. Kostya answers right away.
'The man is sick, and it is freezing outside.' The grammar packs 'man' and 'cold' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Just an ordinary viral cold, nothing too terrible.' The meaning hinges on 'not' working together with 'viral cold' in spoken Russian.
Он еще и больной, что ли, с ним?
'Wait, so he is sick on top of wearing my coat?' Notice how Russian expresses 'he' and 'him' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
'As the doctors say.' Max anchors the line on 'how', while 'medic' completes the thought.
'With an illness like that, it is better to stay somewhere warm.' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'warm' without extra filler words.
Значит, может мне тоже по помойкам лазить?
'So maybe I should go climbing around the dumpsters too?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'so' and finishing on 'to climb'. Kostya answers right away.
'Oh, come on, Kostik.' The grammar packs 'come on' and 'Kostik' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Это я дала ему твою куртку.
Он еще и больной, что ли, с ним?
Значит, может мне тоже по помойкам лазить?
